what: Adversarial 11-agent audit of backtest/monitor_event_study.py (control fairness, replay correctness, metric honesty). All 7 confirmed findings were FIXED in the harness before the final numbers in docs/MONITOR_EVENT_STUDY.md.

confirmed_findings.title: counterfactual_r books phantom exits on positions already dead on the harness's own M5 path (12/45 action units)
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py lines 260-261 and 283-292 (counterfactual_r), consumed at lines 375-376; enabled by study_unit continuing to assess after the stop touch (lines 177-220, stop_touch_bar recorded at 181-182 with no break)
confirmed_findings.claim: counterfactual_r flattens at the trigger bar's close with no check that the position still exists: when the trigger bar is at/after the M5 bar where the harness's own replayed stop (initial or break-even) was touched, the position is fully closed and the honest counterfactual is baseline_r. Verified by exact reproduction (actual_flatten_sum_r 2.9053926093, control mean 18.184869 both match the JSON): 12 of 45 action units have first_action_i >= stop_touch_bar (e.g. entry 2025-12-12 14:00 books cf -1.623R vs baseline -1.000R; 2025-12-26 16:00 books -0.768R vs -0.287R). Net effect on the actual arm is -1.27R: published actual +2.905R should be about +4.178R. per_unit_deltas_flatten (improved 31 / hurt 13) and cf_be_r are contaminated by the same phantom deltas. The control arm is also affected (3.2% of its picks are post-touch) but there the phantom exits net -0.12R, i.e. they slightly deflate the control.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Does not overturn; the bias runs AGAINST act-mode, so the published comparison slightly overstates the margin but not the verdict. Corrected actual (+4.18R, honest tie rule both arms) is still at percentile 0.000 of the honest control (mean 18.36, p5 14.73) and of every fairer control tested (alive-only mean 21.3, time-capped 20.3, life-fraction-matched 8.26). Headline number and per-unit delta counts should be corrected, conclusion stands.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED by exact reproduction (spread 0.16 from ledger source fallback_spread_points=16.0, window 60): actual_flatten_sum_r = 2.9053926093118503 and control mean = 18.184869259405307 match the published JSON to the last digit, so the instrumented rerun is the same computation.

Core assertions all verified against backtest/monitor_event_study.py:
(1) Mechanism is real and line citations are accurate: study_unit records stop_touch_bar at lines 181-182 and keeps assessing with no break (loop lines 177-220, end_time = final exit + 1h), so first ACTION can land at/after the harness's own replayed stop touch; counterfactual_r (flatten branch lines 260-261, tranche loop 283-292) books exit at the trigger bar's close whenever the ledger exit hour window [H, H+1h) has not fully elapsed, with no check that the position is still alive; consumed at lines 375-376.
(2) Exactly 12 of 45 action units have first_action_i >= stop_touch_bar (measured: 32231>=32231, 41580>=41576, 43277>=43269, 44380>=44380, 45960>=45960, 54501>=54501, 60240>=60233 x3, 62701>=62696, 71427>=71422, 73720>=73720).
(3) Net phantom delta on the actual flatten arm = -1.2775R; corrected actual = +4.1829R (claim: -1.27R / ~+4.178R).
(4) Both named examples reproduce exactly: 2025-12-12 14:00 books cf -1.6234R vs baseline -1.0000R (an impossible fill — a stop-capped position cannot lose more than -1R; trigger 15:55 is after the M5 stop touch, inside the ledger stop's 15:00 hour); 2025-12-26 16:00 books -0.7678R vs -0.2871R — and this one is post-death even per the ledger, since the engine executes weekend flattens at the H1 bar OPEN (ftmo_quant_backtest.py flatten(), non-adverse price = bar.open) at 17:00 while the phantom exit is stamped 17:55, so there is no genuine intra-hour "tie" to break.
(5) cf_be_r is contaminated on the same units (net -1.374R) and per_unit_deltas_flatten is contaminated: published improved/hurt 31/13; honest (post-touch -> baseline) gives 27/5.
(6) Control arm effect confirmed in direction and magnitude: net phantom delta -0.111R per seed (claim -0.12R), i.e. it slightly deflates the control; honest control mean 18.296, p5 14.639 (claim 18.36/14.73 — same ballpark under a slightly different honest-rule definition); corrected actual +4.18R sits at percentile 0.0000 of the honest control, so the claim's own impact assessment ("does not overturn") is also correct.

Refutation grounds fail. Not a mischaracterization (all cited lines behave as described). Not fully a disclosed approximation: the same-hour tie rule (approximation #4) discloses "counterfactual exits win same-hour ties (stop-first pessimism)", but it does not cover booking fills worse than the stop on positions the harness's own M5 replay has already stopped out (stop_touch_bar disambiguates the ordering and is ignored), nor exits after open-stamped weekend flattens where no timing ambiguity exists. And it demonstrably biases the control comparison itself, asymmetrically: -1.28R on the actual arm vs -0.11R on the control mean (ACTION clusters at stop touches; uniform random picks rarely do), widening the published actual-vs-control gap by ~1.17R and distorting the improved/hurt counts.

Minor claim inaccuracies that do not affect confirmation: the control post-touch pick incidence is 7.83% of action-unit picks (6.77% with nonzero delta), not the stated 3.2% — but the load-bearing control-side number (net ~-0.12R deflation) is right; and their honest-control mean/p5 differ from mine by ~0.06-0.09R, immaterial to the percentile-0.000 conclusion. Severity is correctly capped at P2: the defect biases AGAINST act-mode, so correcting it (+2.91R -> +4.18R actual) still leaves the monitor's timing at the 0th percentile of every control variant; the headline number, cf_be_r, and the 31/13 delta counts should be corrected, but the adverse-selection verdict stands.

confirmed_findings.title: Replay never terminates at position death: 58% of ACTION bars (255/441) occur after the position is provably closed, contaminating every published metric
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:163 (end_time = final_exit_time + 1h) and :177 (loop has no break at stop touch or ledger exit); downstream at :256-261 and :283-292 (counterfactual_r books flattens of already-dead positions)
confirmed_findings.claim: study_unit keeps calling assess() until final_exit_time+1h with no termination when the unit dies. I reproduced the run bit-exactly (441 action bars, actual flatten +2.9054R, control mean 18.1849, percentile 0.0) and computed exact death boundaries: 234 ACTION bars fire at/after the M5 bar that touched the initial/BE stop on units whose ledger last reason is 'stop' (exact stop model, no trail approximation involved), and 21 fire after a weekend flatten's hour-open. Live, the monitor cannot run on a closed position. 13 of 45 action units have their FIRST action post-death; counterfactual_r then assigns them physically impossible exits (flatten below an already-filled stop) instead of the baseline. This is not among the harness's disclosed approximations. Corrected feasible-only numbers: ACTION stop-touch precision 0.215 vs base 0.0073 (lift ~30x, not 19x, both published numbers wrong on both sides), and the act-on-first-feasible-ACTION flatten counterfactual is +4.18R, not +2.91R.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Does not overturn either conclusion but requires correcting the published numbers. Claim (1)'s stop-touch lift survives and strengthens (19x understated; feasible lift ~30x). Claim (2)'s actual improvement is understated by ~1.3R (+4.18R vs +2.91R), yet even the corrected actual remains at the 0th percentile of the feasibility-corrected uniform control (mean +20.97R, p5 +17.35R), so the kill-decision direction is unchanged.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED by code reading plus bit-exact independent reproduction. Code: monitor_event_study.py line 163 sets end_time = final_exit_time + 1h and the replay loop (lines 177-220) records stop_touch_bar but never breaks at stop touch or ledger exit, so assess() keeps firing on provably closed positions; counterfactual_r (lines 256-261, 283-292) books flattens of dead positions at prices below the already-filled stop (published per-unit rows show cf_flatten_r of -1.623/-1.071/-1.060 vs -1.0 baseline — physically impossible fills). Not disclosed: neither the docstring approximations (lines 21-35) nor the JSON 'approximations' list mentions post-death monitoring; the same-hour tie-break and post-TP2-trail disclosures cover neither the precision-metric contamination nor post-death first-ACTION triggers (and the claim's counts exclude trail-approximated units). Reproduction (spread 0.16, window 60, same ledger/data): published numbers match bit-exactly (441 action bars, actual flatten +2.905393, control mean 18.1849, percentile 0.0); post-death ACTION bars = 234 (at/after M5 initial/BE stop touch, last-reason-'stop' units) + 21 (at/after weekend flatten hour-open) = 255/441 = 58%, exactly as claimed; 13 of 45 action units have first ACTION post-death, exactly as claimed; feasible-only precision 0.2151 vs base 0.00726 (29.6x lift) matches claim (0.215/0.0073/~30x); feasible first-ACTION flatten +4.1777R matches claim (+4.18 vs published +2.91). Only divergence: the feasibility-corrected control mean/p5 (my definition gives 14.44/11.46 vs claim's 20.97/17.35 — a definitional variant of how the corrected control is constructed), but the corrected actual sits at the 0.0 percentile under both definitions, so the claim's stated impact (published numbers wrong on both sides of both metrics, kill-decision direction unchanged) holds regardless. The claim does not mischaracterize the code and is not a disclosed approximation.

confirmed_findings.title: Random-trigger control is hindsight-conditioned: it samples bars BEFORE the first ACTION on units only known ex post to be in the action cohort, so the '0th percentile / adversely selected timing' statistic compares against an infeasible policy
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:427-441, esp. :437 (rng.choice(row["_timeline"]) over the unit's entire monitored life, gated only on n_action>0)
confirmed_findings.claim: The control picks a uniform bar over the whole monitored life of units that ever fired ACTION. At any pre-alert bar, a live policy cannot know the unit belongs to the action cohort (first ACTION fires near the end of losing units' lives; action-unit baseline is -15.5R vs +13.4R for no-action units), so the control smuggles the monitor's own cohort-selection signal into infeasibly early exits. Re-running the control with the information-matched pool (random bar at/after the first ACTION, same 500-seed scheme) yields mean +2.67R with the actual (+2.91R) at the 58th percentile; with post-death bars removed from both sides (first feasible ACTION, +4.18R actual) the feasible timing null has mean +6.15R and the actual sits at the 2.4th percentile. The published '0th percentile of 500 seeds, ACTION fires at local lows' is therefore an artifact of the comparator, not a measurement of timing skill vs chance given the monitor's information set: timing-given-alert ranges from indistinguishable to mildly adverse (~2R aggregate), not pathological.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Corrects the mechanism claim but does not rescue act-mode: a fully feasible, signal-free control I ran (flatten every one of the 70 units at a uniformly random feasible bar, no cohort knowledge) still averages +14.1R (p5 +9.9R), dwarfing act-mode's +2.9R/+4.2R, and the feasible uniform control on action units averages +21.0R with actual at percentile 0.000. So conclusion (2)'s substance - the apparent improvement is exposure reduction in a losing window, not monitor timing skill - survives the strongest fair test; only the '0th percentile / adversely selected at local lows' framing and its supporting statistic must be restated.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. I reproduced the study pipeline exactly (baseline -2.114569R, actual flatten +2.905393R, shipped control mean +18.185R / p5 +14.466 / p95 +22.350 / actual percentile 0.000 — all match backtest/results/XAUUSD_monitor_event_study.json to 6 decimals), then verified every predicate of the claim. (1) Code predicate is accurate: monitor_event_study.py:436 gates the control on row["n_action"] > 0 (cohort membership knowable only ex post) and :437 draws rng.choice(row["_timeline"]) over the unit's ENTIRE monitored life, including pre-first-ACTION bars. (2) Hindsight conditioning is material, not cosmetic: action units' baseline is -15.55R vs +13.43R for no-action units (exactly the claim's -15.5/+13.4), and on average 79.6% (median 83.5%) of each action unit's sampling pool lies strictly BEFORE its first ACTION — bars where no alert-gated policy can act. The +18.2R null location is therefore dominated by infeasible early exits that harvest loss-avoidance only available with cohort foreknowledge. (3) The claim's headline re-run reproduces EXACTLY: an information-matched control (uniform bar at/after first ACTION, same 500 seeds 1_000_000+i) yields mean +2.672R with the actual (+2.905R) at percentile 0.580 — i.e., the monitor's first-ACTION timing is statistically indistinguishable from random feasible timing given the alert. A stricter pre-stop-touch feasible pool gives mean +3.82R with actual at the 10th percentile (their variant with a different death definition reported 2.4th pct / +6.15R mean; secondary numbers vary with pool definition but every feasible variant collapses the null from +18.2R to ~+2.7-6.2R and moves the actual off the 0th percentile, landing in the claim's stated 'indistinguishable to mildly adverse' band). (4) This is not a disclosed approximation: the docstring (lines 21-36) and the 'approximations' output (lines 547-553) cover stop modeling, spread, tranche weights, H1 tie-stamping, and EMA seeding — nothing about the control's conditioning — and the bias affects the control comparison itself. (5) The construct-validity point stands: a null whose mass is ~80% pre-alert bars on deeply losing units cannot be beaten by ANY alert-gated policy, even one with perfect timing given the monitor's information set, so 'actual at the 0th percentile of 500 seeds' measures 'not an oracle,' not 'adversely selected timing.' The published mechanism statistic is a comparator artifact exactly as claimed. Caveats that do NOT rescue the harness: (a) the claim's own impact concession is verified — a fully feasible signal-free policy (flatten all 70 units at a uniform random bar, no monitor) averages +11.3R in my reproduction (+14.1R under their pool definition), dwarfing act-mode's +2.9R, so conclusion (2)'s substance (improvement = exposure reduction in a losing window, act-mode adds no timing value) survives and the kill decision is unaffected; (b) 'fires at local lows near the stop' retains independent support (within-unit percentile mean 0.25/median 0.19, 19x stop-touch precision, and mild adverse signal in pre-death feasible nulls), so only the 0th-percentile statistic and the 'pathologically adverse' framing must be restated — but the specific defect alleged (hindsight-conditioned control producing an artifactual 0th-percentile statistic at :427-441) is real, code-grounded, and quantitatively confirmed, including an exact match of the claim's +2.67R / 58th-percentile re-run.

confirmed_findings.title: Band-breach precision measures a close-volatility 2-sigma projection against next-2-bar intrabar extremes, and the 'no lift on band breach' leg flips sign once post-death bars are removed
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:410-412 (hit_band vs forward_extreme) with :231-238 (forward_extreme uses bar lows / highs+spread), vs lower_tf_monitor.py:134-141 (projected_adverse is a close-return-volatility band)
confirmed_findings.claim: projected_adverse is a 2-sigma band on closes derived from close-to-close return volatility, but the harness scores a 'breach' if any intrabar extreme (plus spread for shorts) crosses it within 2 bars - a basis mismatch that inflates breach frequency, relatively more on quiet (base) bars where the band is narrow. Published: 0.084 given ACTION vs 0.091 base ('no lift'). Removing the post-death bars of finding 1 (extreme-based measure): 0.113 vs 0.091 - a mild positive lift. Measured on closes, matching the band's own basis: 0.045 vs 0.051 - no lift. The result the PR cites is thus jointly an artifact of contamination plus measurement basis, and the sign depends on which is fixed.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Weakens the second leg of claim (1) as stated: 'NO lift on band breach (0.084 vs 0.091)' is not a robust null - it becomes a mild positive lift under the harness's own extreme-based convention once infeasible bars are excluded. Does not affect the stop-touch lift or the counterfactual/control conclusion; the band metric should be restated as measurement-dependent rather than a clean null.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Code verification: projected_adverse (lower_tf_monitor.py:134-141) is a 2-sigma band on the last M5 close derived from close-to-close return volatility (_return_sigma, lines 114-127), while the harness scores a breach at monitor_event_study.py:410-412 using forward_extreme (lines 231-238), which takes the intrabar adverse extreme (min low for longs, max high+spread for shorts) over the next 2 bars — the basis mismatch is real and is NOT among the disclosed approximations (docstring lines 21-34, output lines 547-553); neither is the post-death timeline contamination (study_unit monitors to final_exit_time+1h past the stop touch, line 177). Empirical reproduction (spread 0.16, window 60, XAUUSD ledger; published JSON replicated exactly — band 0.0839 vs 0.0905, stop 0.4558 vs 0.0238): (a) close-basis measurement on all bars gives 0.0454 vs 0.0506, matching the claim's '0.045 vs 0.051 — no lift' to the third decimal; (b) excluding post-death bars (i >= stop_touch_bar) under the harness's own extreme-based convention gives 0.1198 vs 0.0910 (ledger-stop-units variant: 0.1111 vs 0.0908), confirming the claimed '0.113 vs 0.091 mild positive lift' within definitional wiggle — every stop-touch-anchored exclusion variant lands at 0.101-0.129 vs ~0.091, all positive; 249/441 ACTION bars (56%) are post-death. Extreme basis inflates base breach frequency ~1.8x (0.0905 vs 0.0506) as claimed. The claim's scoping is accurate: stop-touch lift survives decontamination massively (0.208 vs 0.007) and the counterfactual/random-control conclusion is unaffected. Minor imprecisions — the 'relatively more on quiet bars' mechanism only holds cleanly on the decontaminated sample (full-sample inflation is ~equal: base 1.79x vs ACTION 1.85x), and the post-exclusion lift is within binomial noise (z ≈ 1.0-1.4) — do not overturn the core finding, which the claim itself states conservatively ('mild positive lift', 'restate as measurement-dependent rather than a clean null'). The published 'NO lift on band breach (0.084 vs 0.091)' is indeed a joint artifact of measurement basis plus post-death contamination, and its sign is convention-dependent.

confirmed_findings.title: Counterfactuals and precision metrics include post-stop-touch (dead-trade) bars; actual policy charged impossible exits
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:163,177 (timeline runs to final_exit+1h, past the M5 stop touch); :241-293 (counterfactual_r never checks trigger_i vs stop_touch_bar); :375-376,437-438 (cf and control use triggers unconditionally); :407-419 (precision loop over all timeline bars)
confirmed_findings.claim: Instrumented re-run (spread 0.16, window 60, reproduces all shipped numbers exactly): 249/441 ACTION bars (56%) fire AT/AFTER the M5 stop-touch bar, and 161 of the 201 ACTION 'hits' (80%) behind the 45.6%/19x precision headline are post-mortem bars where the stop was already touched. Live-bar ACTION precision is 20.8% (40/192) vs live base 0.40%. Worse, 12 of 45 ACTION units have their FIRST ACTION after the stop touch; counterfactual_r flattens already-stopped tranches at the trigger close (below the stop in 4 units, worst -1.62R vs -1.0R baseline), deflating the actual flatten sum by 1.28R (2.91 -> 4.18 corrected). This is the disclosed 'counterfactual wins same-hour ties' rule, but it biases the CONTROL COMPARISON differentially: first-ACTIONs cluster inside the stop-exit hour while uniform random picks land there ~7% of the time, so the pessimism hits the actual policy far harder than the control.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Does NOT overturn the kill. Re-running the control with picks restricted to live (pre-touch) bars and dead triggers reverted to baseline: corrected actual = 4.18R vs control mean 20.86R, min across 500 seeds 14.08R - still 0th percentile (gap ~8 pick-noise sigma); live-only within-unit percentile mean 0.243 (n=33). But conclusion (1)'s '0.456 vs 0.024, 19x' and conclusion (2)'s '+2.9R' are both materially misstated as written; the honest live figures are 0.208 vs 0.004 and +4.18R.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED — could not refute; every falsifiable element of the claim reproduces exactly. I re-ran the full study (ledger=backtest/results/XAUUSD.json, m15/m5 CSVs in backtest/data, spread 0.16, window 60) importing the harness's own functions, first reproducing all shipped numbers bit-for-bit (441 ACTION bars, 0.455782 vs 0.023829 stop-touch, 0.083900 vs 0.090534 band, actual flatten 2.9054R, control mean 18.1849, p5 14.4656), which validates the instrumentation. The instrumented counts then match the claim exactly: 249/441 ACTION bars fire at/after the unit's M5 stop-touch bar; 161 of the 201 ACTION stop-touch 'hits' behind the 45.6%/19x headline are post-touch bars; live-bar ACTION precision is 40/192 = 20.83%; 12/45 ACTION units have their first ACTION at/after the stop touch; exactly 4 of those flatten below the stop (cf_flatten -1.0137, -1.0603, -1.0710, -1.6234 — all visible in the shipped JSON); reverting dead first-ACTIONs to baseline moves the actual flatten sum 2.9054 → 4.1829 (+1.2775R ≈ the claimed 1.28R); the live-picks-only control gives mean 20.8622, min 14.0819 across 500 seeds with corrected-actual percentile 0.0000; live-only within-unit percentile mean 0.2434, n=33. The claim's '~7%' random dead-pick rate also verifies (7.84%). Code citations are accurate: study_unit's loop (lines 177-220) runs to final_exit_time+1h (line 163) and records stop_touch_bar (180-182) but never stops assessing; counterfactual_r (241-293) never consults stop_touch_bar; precision (406-419) and cf/control (375-376, 437-438) consume those bars/triggers unconditionally. The refutation escape hatches all fail: (a) the code is not 'correct' — the harness has M5-precise knowledge of its own stop-touch bar (it uses it for the lead-time metric) yet treats knowably-dead bars as actionable in precision/cf/control, and the dead designation is sound because the harness stop (initial→BE) sits at-or-wider than the engine's true stop (unmodelled post-TP2 trail is tighter, per the docstring), so the real position is genuinely dead at/after the harness touch; (b) the disclosed-approximation exclusion does not apply — the precision contamination (56% of ACTION bars, 80% of hits post-mortem) is disclosed nowhere in the docstring or 'approximations' output, and the same-hour-tie rule, while disclosed, demonstrably biases the control comparison differentially (26.7% of actual first-ACTION triggers are dead vs 7.8% of uniform random picks; the actual arm is understated by 44% of its corrected value vs 13% for the control arm). Two trivial deviations, neither refuting: the claim's 'live base 0.40%' corresponds to live non-ACTION bars (46/11611 = 0.396%; including live ACTION bars gives 86/11803 = 0.729% — either way the shipped 2.38% base and 19x lift are misstated, and the live lift is actually larger, 29-53x); and 'pessimism hits the actual policy far harder than the control' is true in trigger frequency and relative understatement, though in absolute sum-R the correction moved the control mean more (+2.68 vs +1.28) — which only strengthens the claim's own bottom line. The claimed impact is also accurate: corrected actual 4.18R remains at the 0th percentile of the corrected control (min 14.08R), so the adverse-selection kill stands; conclusions (1) and (2) are materially misstated as written but not overturned.

confirmed_findings.title: The 19x stop-touch lift is stop-proximity mechanics, not monitor skill: zero lift once matched on the monitor's own touch probability
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:399-419 (base = all 12,128 monitored bars incl. ACTION bars and bars with 2.5-ATR/far-BE stops); backtest/lower_tf_monitor.py:200-202 (ACTION = M15 misalignment AND threat, where threat = divergence OR band_breach OR touch_prob>=0.50 - the latter two are direct functions of distance-to-stop and vol)
confirmed_findings.claim: The literal circularity hypothesis is partly wrong - only 137/441 ACTION bars pass the touch_prob>=0.5 gate (mean ACTION touch_prob 0.372) - but the deeper defect is confirmed: matched on the monitor's own MC touch_prob and restricted to live bars, ACTION adds NO lift over non-ACTION bars (tp 0.05-0.15: 22.4% vs 20.0%; tp 0.15-0.25: 30.4% vs 33.3%; tp>=0.5 incl. dead bars: 95.6% vs 96.6%; tp 0.25-0.5: 50.6% vs non-action 66.7%). The base rate is also diluted by ~11.6k bars where the stop is mechanically unreachable in 10 minutes (live non-action base 0.40%). A fair skill claim would require matched distance-to-stop/touch_prob strata on live bars - which shows the divergence/EMA-misalignment components contribute nothing to short-horizon stop-touch prediction.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Overturns the pro-monitor half of conclusion (1) ('ACTION lifts stop-touch probability 19x'): the lift is fully attributable to mechanical stop proximity, so ACTION is a stop-proximity detector with no incremental predictive skill. This STRENGTHENS the kill and also weakens the doc's 'alert mode viable' recommendation, which rests on the same contaminated 19x figure.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed, not refuted. (1) Code mechanics match the claim: monitor_event_study.py:406-419 increments base_n on every timeline bar (all 12,128 bars including the 441 ACTION bars and dead post-stop-touch bars, since study_unit keeps assessing until final_exit_time+1h), and lower_tf_monitor.py:183-185,200-202 make ACTION = M15 misalignment AND (divergence OR band_breach OR tp>=0.5), where band_breach and tp are direct functions of distance-to-stop in recent-vol units. (2) Every cited number reproduced exactly by re-running the study (spread 0.16, window 60; totals match the published JSON): 137/441 ACTION bars with tp>=0.5, mean ACTION tp 0.3722, live strata 22.41% vs 20.0% (tp 0.05-0.15) and 30.43% vs 33.33% (tp 0.15-0.25), all-bars 50.62% vs 66.67% (tp 0.25-0.5) and 95.62% vs 96.55% (tp>=0.5), 11,611 live non-ACTION bars at 0.396% realized touch. Realized touch is monotone in the monitor's own tp (0.3% at tp<0.05 -> 96% at tp>=0.5), so the 19x lift is composition on stop proximity. (3) Attempted refutation via the stratum the auditor omitted (live tp<0.05: ACTION 6.90% vs 0.31%) fails: decomposed, tp==0 gives ACTION 0/44 vs 0.13% (the pure EMA/divergence bars never touch), and the 0<tp<0.05 gap (13.95% vs 5.80%) tracks finer proximity (ACTION median z-distance 4.1 vs 10.7 band-units); matched on z, ACTION is at-or-below non-ACTION in z[0,1) (50% vs 75%) and z[1,1.5) (28% vs 37%), above only in z[1.5,2) (13.6% vs 0%, small n) — no consistent incremental lift. (4) Not a disclosed approximation: the docstring discloses the all-bars base-rate design but not its confounding, and the defect targets the skill interpretation of claimed conclusion (1). Minor imprecision only: the auditor's 0.25-0.5 figures use all-bars conditioning while other strata are live-only, but each number matches the code under its stated conditioning and the conclusion is unchanged: ACTION is a stop-proximity detector with no incremental short-horizon stop-touch skill.

confirmed_findings.title: The '+2.9R vs -2.1R improvement' is statistically indistinguishable from zero and concentrated in 2 units; harness reports sums with no dispersion
confirmed_findings.location: backtest/monitor_event_study.py:463-476 (bucket() reports sum/mean/DD only), :517-529 (per_unit_deltas_flatten reports counts and a median diluted by 26 no-action units)
confirmed_findings.claim: Per-unit flatten deltas (n=70): mean +0.072R, sd 0.359, t = 1.67 (p~0.10 two-sided) BEFORE accounting for time-clustered units (e.g. 3-4 simultaneous stop-outs on 2025-09-23/24, 11-11/13, 12-12), which lowers effective significance further. The top 2 units (+1.15R, +1.06R - both dead-trigger artifacts per finding 1) contribute 44% of the +5.02R total delta. The reported median_delta_r = 0.0 is computed over all 70 units including 26 with no ACTION, making it uninformative about the acted-on population.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_conclusion: Cuts the last pro-act-mode leg of conclusion (2): 'acting on ACTION improves aggregate outcome vs baseline' is unsupported even before the random control - the improvement never clears significance. Kill conclusion reinforced from a second direction.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED — every quantitative assertion in the claim reproduces exactly from the study's own output, and the cited code lines do what the claim says.

Code anchors verified (monitor_event_study.py): bucket() at lines 464-476 emits only sum_r / mean_r / max_dd_r per bucket — no sd, CI, or any test statistic anywhere in the output; per_unit_deltas_flatten at lines 517-529 emits only changed/improved/hurt counts plus median_delta_r computed at 527-529 over ALL of per_unit (all 70 units), not the acted-on subpopulation. Not a disclosed approximation: the approximations list (lines 547-553 and docstring) covers stop modeling, spread, tie-breaking, gross-R weights, and EMA seeding — nothing about missing inferential statistics.

Numbers recomputed from backtest/results/XAUUSD_monitor_event_study.json: per-unit flatten deltas n=70, mean +0.0717R, sd 0.3590, t=1.671, exact two-sided p=0.0993 — matches the claim's +0.072/0.359/1.67/p~0.10 to the digit. Top 2 deltas are +1.155R (2025-10-20 unit) and +1.060R (2026-06-24 unit), summing to 2.215R = 44.1% of the +5.02R total delta — matches the claimed 44%. median_delta_r=0.0 is confirmed diluted: 26 of 70 units have exactly-zero delta (25 with no ACTION per the JSON's own units_with_any_action=45, plus 1 acted-on unit with zero delta — the claim's "26 with no ACTION" is off by one but immaterial; the dilution mechanism is exactly as described, and the acted-on median is actually +0.155R). Time clustering is real: acted-on units share entry days (2025-12-12 has 3 units; 2025-09-23, 11-11, 11-13 each have 2), so the iid t-stat overstates significance, as claimed. An independent bootstrap of the aggregate delta (10k unit resamples) gives 95% CI [−0.90R, +10.77R] with 4.85% of resamples ≤ 0 — i.e., two-sided ~0.10, independently confirming the aggregate improvement does not clear conventional significance even before clustering.

Refutation attempts that failed: nonparametric direction tests are significant (sign test 31 improved vs 13 hurt, p=0.0096; Wilcoxon on nonzero deltas p=0.018), but these test per-unit direction, not the aggregate-R claim under attack — conclusion (2)'s "+2.9R vs −2.1R" is a sum, governed by the mean, and the sum's distribution is dominated by fat tails (top-2 = 44%, worst single delta −1.47R), which is precisely the claim's concentration point. The mean-based t and the bootstrap of the sum both land at p~0.10. So the pro-act leg "acting on ACTION improves aggregate outcome vs baseline" is genuinely unsupported at conventional significance by the harness's own data, and the harness's output provides no dispersion information that would reveal this, while its one distribution stat (median_delta_r=0.0) is uninformative by construction. Legitimate P2 metrics-and-stats defect; it reinforces (does not bias) the random-control kill conclusion.

refuted_titles: '0th percentile of 500 seeds' quantifies only pick-randomization noise, not sampling uncertainty - but the gap survives clustering-adjusted per-unit inference
